items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: Junior Cobb come in and heard me play, and he went out and told Hugh Swiffer by it, well he's the guy that had the band.

ctx.x: You never know when a Chinaman died? That's what I heard. It's disappeared, huh? Mm-hmm. Do you remember Junie Cobb?

That's the man who got me the job at Jeffrey Tabin. Two brothers, Junie Cobb and Jimmy Cobb. I was playing after, this was before I went to Golden Lily though, I just went to Chicago with the show, Mac and Mac. And we was playing at a little place called Bookstore. I tell you, her wife was playing the piano. Uh, what did this boy play so much piano? Played with us a long time. Tenny Wilson. Tenny Wilson. He had a little girl named Aurene, who was his wife. Good piano player. So she heard about me, she come and…
Law grab her and went in there and got all that stuff out of front of them. Yeah, Gene Carver got me a great job.

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1959-09-01
items.q: The only band I sat down and read music with, best I could, was Tiny Pond and Jelly Roll Morton and Huey Swift.

ctx.x: Punch, in 1919, when you first got here, what did the brass bands play like? Were they strictly music? Were they here?

No, they played more marches then. But I'm going to tell you now, I ain't going to lie to you. Hick was a very few men's in them bands reading. Like the trumpet players be reading. But them other guys were just speaking. I mean, you know, using their brains. They could hear a tune and play it. That's right. Yeah. That's right. Now you take men like Joe Howard, and them men that were playing. They had their music up. They were playing it, see? But they had men on trombone, men on alto, and things like that. They…
Well, what about Louie? Did you ever work with him?
